newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end flat ahead of holiday start.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end flat ahead of holiday start.

text.p: Singapore shares ended flat on Wednesday in muted trade as dealers hunkered down on the sidelines in anticipation of a long Lunar New Year lay-off that starts after the lunchtime close on Thursday.
"There's nothing really happening out there," one dealer said.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended the day mildly firmer at 2,195.78, up 3.56 points.
Volume was moderate with 186.48 million units traded, but provided wins for most with gainers ahead of losers 242 to 109.
Malaysian stocks traded over the counter in Singapore generated the heaviest interest among dealers, as reflected by a rise in the UOB-OTC index, which closed up 8.70 at 1,287.91.

Malaysia's MBF Holdings was Wednesday's most traded share, accounting for almost 10 percent of market volume at 14.9 million to rise Singapore $0.05 to S$0.825 (US$0.585). Other well-traded Malaysian shares included Berjaya Industrial and Promet Bhd.
Creative Technology, Tuesday's top loser, led Wednesday gainers up S$0.60 at S$19.60 on light volume. The foreign share tranche of DBS Bank slipped S$0.50 to S$19.00.
